atoms.b: School pressure has affected students across all generations. Exam stress and university admissions anxiety were serious concerns decades ago. ((++Similarly ++Likewise)), students today face multiple additional pressures. They worry about grades, university costs, career uncertainty, and whether their degree will even be relevant in five years. ((++In_comparison_with)) their parents, lots of young adults also work part-time while studying to afford life expenses. ((++Equally)) heavy is the psychological burden. ((++Likewise ++Similarly)), some studies suggest depression and anxiety among teenagers have reached record levels.

atoms.b: Climate change creates a unique psychological burden for young people. Previous generations worried about war or economic recession. ((++Like)) them, Gen Z kids grow up knowing the planet itself is in crisis. ((++In_comparison_with)) older generations, whose actions are a source of this problem, young people are expected to solve it. The weight of this responsibility is ((++equally)) real, comparable to the physical impacts of climate change. ((++Likewise)), environmental scientists and mental health professionals have identified “climate anxiety” as a growing mental health concern among teenagers.

atoms.b: Teenagers construct online identities with the same care their parents once applied to clothing and hairstyles. Just ((++like)) physical appearance was once the primary way teenagers communicated identity, social media presence is now also of importance. A carefully curated feed or social media presence can feel ((++equally ++similarly)) important to self-worth as grades or popularity once did. The pressure to maintain a perfect online image can affect mental health. ((++Similarly ++Equally)), studies show that teenagers who spend more time on social media report higher rates of anxiety and lower self-esteem.
